content: It appears to be a comprehensive list of pharmacological interactions, including mechanisms of action, recommendations for monitoring, dose adjustments, and contraindications. 1. Ketoconazole increases the plasma levels of indacaterol (inhaled) by modulating both P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and CYP3A4 activities. No dose adjustment is required at the 75 mcg dose, but caution and monitoring are advised. 2. The combination of indapamide and ketoconazole is contraindicated due to their additive effects on prolonging the QTc interval. 3. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of indinavir by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and affecting CYP3A4-mediated hepatic and intestinal metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 4. Indinavir may also increase the levels of ketoconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, but the clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 5. Ketoconazole significantly increases the levels and effects of infigratinib (DSC) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The use of alternative drugs is recommended. 6. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of irinotecan by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and reducing its metabolism. The use of alternative drugs is strongly recommended. 7. UGT1A1 inhibitors, such as ketoconazole, decrease the metabolism of irinotecan, further increasing its levels and effects. Avoidance or substitution with alternative drugs is advised. 8. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of irinotecan liposomal by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and reducing its metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 9. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 10. Isoniazid decreases the levels of ketoconazole through an unspecified mechanism, but it may also increase ketoconazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 11. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of isradipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 12. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of istradefylline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. The istradefylline dose should not exceed 20 mg/day when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 13. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of itraconazole by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. The use of alternative drugs is recommended. 14. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of ivabradine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 15. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of ivacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of ivacaftor is required when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 16. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of ivermectin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of ivosidenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The use of alternative drugs is recommended. If coadministration is unavoidable, the ivosidenib dose should be reduced to 250 mg daily. 18. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of ixabepilone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The use of alternative drugs is recommended. 19. Ketoconazole increases the levels of lacosamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required, especially in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 20. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of lansoprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lansoprazole decreases ketoconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents, and alternative drugs are recommended. 21. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of lapatinib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. The use of alternative drugs is recommended. 22. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of larotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, the larotrectinib dose should be reduced by 50%. 23. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of lefamulin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The use of alternative drugs is recommended. 24. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is not recommended. 25. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of lenacapavir by inhibiting P-gp, UGT1A1, and CYP3A4 metabolism. The use of alternative drugs is recommended. 26. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of leniolisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The use of alternative drugs is recommended. 27. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of lesinurad (DSC) by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 28. Ketoconazole increases the effects of letermovir by reducing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 29. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of levamlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 30. Ketoconazole and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 31. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of levomilnacipran by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The levomilnacipran dose should not exceed 80 mg/day when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 32. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. 33. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of linagliptin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 34. Ketoconazole and lofepramine both prolong the QTc interval. The use of alternative drugs is recommended. 35. Ketoconazole increases the levels of lomitapide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to a significant increase in lomitapide levels. 36. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of lonafarnib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 37. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of loperamide by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 38. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ketoconazole doses >200 mg/day are not recommended when used with lopinavir/ritonavir. 39. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of loratadine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 40. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of lorlatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, the lorlatinib dose should be reduced by 25 mg/day. 41. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of losartan by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism, potentially reducing its conversion to the active metabolite E-3174. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 42. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of lovastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This combination is contraindicated due to the increased risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. 43. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of lumacaftor/ivacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 44. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of lurasidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 45. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of lurbinectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, the lurbinectedin dose should be reduced by 50%. 46. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of macimorelin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The use of alternative drugs is recommended. 47. Ketoconazole increases the levels and effects of macitentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The use of alternative drugs is recommended.
